title: Check yourself: what the compiler says about throw and throws

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, what does the compiler do when an unchecked exception is listed in a method's `throws` clause?

options.text: It rejects the clause, since that list is meant for checked types
options.says: The page says listing an unchecked exception there is allowed.

options.text: It makes each caller catch that exception or declare it as well
options.says: The page says the compiler does not enforce the clause for unchecked exceptions.

options.text: It accepts the clause as documentation and enforces nothing
options.says: The page says the listing is allowed and documents the exception, but the compiler does not enforce it.

questions.stem: Per this page, how does the compiler treat a statement written directly after a `throw` in the same block?

options.text: It accepts it, and that statement runs once a catch clause handles the exception
options.says: Control never returns to the block after a throw; the page says the compiler rejects such a statement.

options.text: It reports an error, because that statement can never be reached
options.says: The page lists this under its key points: the statement is unreachable and the compiler rejects it.

options.text: It accepts it, and that statement runs before the exception leaves the method
options.says: Only finally blocks run on the way out; the page says the compiler rejects the statement.

concepts: Listing an unchecked exception in throws documents it, but the compiler enforces nothing.
A statement directly after a throw in the same block is unreachable and does not compile.
